verses.text: Hera grew furious and quarreled with her husband.
From this quarrel she bore a glorious son,
Hephaestus, without making love with Zeus, who carries the aegis,
whose skill with his hands surpassed that of all the heavenly gods.
But Zeus lay with the daughter of Oceanus and lovely-haired Tethys,
a girl with lovely cheeks, away from Hera,
deceiving Metis, though she knew so many tricks.
He seized her in his hands and put her inside his belly,
afraid she might bear another child stronger than his thunderbolt.
That was why Zeus, son of Cronus, enthroned on high and living in the upper air,
suddenly swallowed her. At once she conceived Pallas Athena,
whom the father of gods and humans brought to birth
from his head, beside the banks of the river Triton.
Metis stayed hidden beneath the organs inside Zeus’s body,
Athena’s mother, shaping what is right,
knowing more than all the gods and mortal humans.
There the goddess had found a place; from there her handiwork surpassed
that of all the immortals who live in the halls of Olympus,
[having made the aegis, Athena’s armor that sends armies fleeing.]
With it, Zeus brought her to birth wearing her battle gear.
